archimate:Goal.name: Longitudinal Care Coordination - Ongoing coordination of care activities across time, settings, and disciplines
archimate:Goal.documentation:
The "Longitudinal Care Coordination" goal is a long-term clinical strategy focused on continuously managing and aligning a patient's healthcare journey across all providers, settings, and health events over their entire lifespan or an extended course of treatment.
Its purpose is to transition from fragmented, episodic care to a cohesive, continuous health management model that proactively supports patients with complex or chronic conditions through every stage of their health journey.
Example: A health system achieves this goal by assigning a dedicated coordinator to a patient with multiple sclerosis to manage their transitions between neurology visits, physical therapy, home health, and occasional hospital stays over several decades.
